title: Eternal Punishment
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Eternal punishment is the final and everlasting judgment of God against those who remain outside Christ. Scripture teaches that the destiny of the wicked is not temporary correction, but conscious and eternal judgment.
summary: Eternal punishment is the final and everlasting judgment of God against those who remain outside Christ. Scripture teaches that the destiny of the wicked is not temporary correction, but conscious and eternal judgment.
christFocus: Jesus Christ warns of eternal punishment and offers Himself as the only Savior from judgment. His cross reveals both the seriousness of sin and the mercy available to sinners now.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture speaks soberly about eternal punishment. This doctrine must not be softened because the subject is difficult, nor handled carelessly because the stakes are eternal.

Eternal punishment is the righteous judgment of God against unrepentant sin and unbelief. It is not arbitrary cruelty; it is the holy judgment of the God who is light and justice.

Jesus describes eternal punishment in contrast with eternal life. The same passage that speaks of the righteous entering life also speaks of the wicked entering punishment.

This doctrine is closely related to hell, the lake of fire, and the second death. It reminds the church that the Gospel is urgent because judgment is real and final.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
If eternal punishment is minimized, people may lose the urgency of repentance and the weight of what Christ saves from. The cross becomes sentimental rather than saving.

This doctrine should make believers compassionate, not proud. No one should speak of eternal punishment lightly. The truth should move the church to prayer, tears, holiness, and Gospel proclamation.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not treat eternal punishment as an embarrassment to hide or a weapon to use harshly. Let Scripture’s warnings drive you to Christ, deepen gratitude for grace, and stir patient, truthful witness to those outside Him.
